title: Preemptible Arbitrator: regional hedging and GPU-type selection for spend-safe routing
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement an "arbitrator" layer that sits between request routing and the capacity allocator to make cost-aware routing decisions that (1) prefer preemptible (preemptible/spot) capacity when safe, (2) select appropriate GPU class by model runtime profile, (3) enforce soft tenant-level budget caps, and (4) provide graceful degradation via a chain of fallback model variants. This ticket covers the design, prototype, simulation, and a plan for a staged rollout.
implementation_notes: Arbitrator responsibilities: compute per-request candidate region+instance-class score combining (latency SLO risk, predicted unit-cost, preemption probability, remaining tenant budget, GPU suitability for model), return ranked candidates with routing hints.

Scoring components: latency penalty (based on p95 from region trace), cost estimate (per-token cost derived from kernel + instance price), preemptibility risk (time-decayed probability derived from spot eviction traces), GPU-fit multiplier (memory/throughput compatibility), tenant budget headroom multiplier (soft cap enforcement).

Regional hedging: maintain short-term Bayesian estimate of preemption risk per region/instance-class using evictions and capacity churn; use this to hedge by splitting some fraction of concurrent requests to lower-risk regions when headroom low.

GPU selection: prefer smaller, cheaper GPUs for models with low throughput sensitivity (short inputs) and prefer higher-memory/throughput GPUs for long sequence workloads. Implement a lightweight fingerprinting of recent request length/kv-cache behavior to choose GPU class.

Fallback chain: configure per-model ordered fallback variants (quantized variants, smaller family model, cached-response policy). Arbitrator should attach fallback policy to routed request so that runtime can enact seamless downgrade on preemption or budget breach.

Soft budget enforcement: implement probabilistic admission control — when tenant spending approaches cap, increase latency penalty and prefer cached or cheaper variants instead of hard rejecting. Expose telemetry to customers and provide 'grace window' and override knob for enterprise tenants.

Interfaces: REST config + router API: POST /arbitrator/score returns up to N candidates with metadata (region, instance_class, expected_cost_per_token, preempt_prob, fallback_chain). Router then chooses top candidate and issues work request.

Simulation: run against 30-day production trace anonymized for cost and latency. Compare baseline (current region-pref + simple spot preference) vs arbitrator policies under 3 tenant budget profiles (aggressive, normal, conservative).

Telemetry: emit per-request chosen_score, final_cost_estimate, effective_fallback_used, preempt_event boolean. Surface tenant-facing alerting when arbitration changes behavior due to budget thresholds.
Testing: unit tests for scoring math; e2e on k8s dev cluster with fake preemption events; load test to ensure arbitrator latency < 2ms median under 1k qps.
acceptance_criteria: Arbitrator prototype implements scoring and returns candidate list for all sample requests in test harness.
Simulations show >=18% average per-token cost reduction for 'aggressive spot preference' tenants without increasing latency p95 by >10% in baseline traffic mix.
System respects tenant soft budget caps: when simulated spend hits cap, routed mix shifts towards cached / quantized / smaller variants and recorded spend slope reduces.
No SLO regressions in canary traffic (p95 latency and error rate within existing SLOs) during staged rollout.
Telemetry and dashboards (Console) surfaced for per-tenant arbitrator decisions and preempt events.
Design doc and API spec merged in Confluence and API repo; at least one integration PR opened referencing this ticket.
Security review completed for budget enforcement paths (no tenant data leakage in scoring telemetry).
rollout_plan: Week 1: implement proto service + scoring library; internal demo and run unit simulations against trace.
Week 2: add fallback-chain wiring and tenant headroom logic; run extended simulations and perf tests.
Week 3: Canary rollout to 2% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants with 'spot-allowed' flag; monitor cost, p95 latency, preemptions.
Week 4: Expand to 10% traffic; add dashboard panels and customer-facing notices; run emergency rollback test.
Week 5: Opt-in beta for enterprise tenants with enforced reporting and override; collect feedback and tune scoring weights.
Post-beta: prepare release notes and SDK docs; enable default for new tenants behind feature flag.
metrics: per_token_cost_estimate_delta: delta between arbitrator estimate and actual cost
tenant_spend_rate: spend per min per tenant (used to check soft cap behavior)
fallback_ratio: percent requests that used a fallback variant
preempt_event_rate: preemptions per 10k requests by region/instance
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: scoring model mis-estimates preempt probability leading to higher user-visible errors. Mitigation: conservative default weights and simulated stress tests; provide emergency circuit-breaker to prefer non-preemptible capacity.

Risk: increased router complexity adds latency. Mitigation: keep arbitrator decision path in-memory cache for frequent prompts and use a small sketch (LRU) for repeat users; target median decision latency < 2ms.
Risk: tenant confusion about soft caps triggering fallbacks. Mitigation: customer-facing dashboard + email alerts and clear documentation of graceful degradation behaviors and override settings.

Risk: potential billing edge-cases if fallback uses cheaper model but upstream logs attribute to the original model. Mitigation: ensure billing uses runtime-executed-variant metadata and update billing pipeline if necessary.
Risk: regional regulatory constraints (data locality) preventing hedging. Mitigation: honor data region policy as a hard constraint in candidate scoring.
Risk: inaccurate GPU-fit fingerprinting causing throughput regressions. Mitigation: start with conservative mapping rules and collect perf telemetry to refine over 2 cycles.
